acceptance_criteria: CRITICAL CONTEXT -- R-Co IS REACHABLE THIS SESSION, unlike the first S6 batch. ORCH verified `ls c:/Users/tvolo/dev/ai-dala/R-Co/src/` succeeds and confirmed real line counts. (b) R-Co design docs exist for essentially every one: src/design/scheduler.md, scheduler-concurrency-epic3.md, iss0618-scheduler-lock-and-error-signaling.md, exp-05-secrets-module.md, fix-iss0112-secret-ref.md, iss-0076-secrets-table-migration-fix.md, oidc-21-zero-downtime-secret-rotation.md, obs-01-structured-logging.md, obs-02-prometheus-metrics.md, obs-03-audit-log.md, obs-04-instance-timeline.md, obs-06-alerting-hooks.md, adp-09-tamper-evident-audit-chain.md, repository.md, plc-01-process-module-catalog.md, expr.md, expr-types.md, expr-cutover-exp102.md, ord-03-sequence-order-guard-gap-sweeping.md. Decompose along these behavioural seams (R-Co's own requirement ids), NOT 1:1 per Zig file -- src/expr/mod.zig alone is 2370 lines and src/scheduler/scheduler.zig is 1336, so a file-per-requirement mapping would produce oversized entries. This is the same rule the S3 and S5 expansions followed.

EXISTING LETFLOW COVERAGE -- ORCH surveyed this; honour it rather than re-porting what is already done. (1) EXPRESSIONS: lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex ALREADY EXISTS (REQ-050 done S3, audited by REQ-111 done S3) -- a real tokenizer+parser+evaluator covering variable refs, 6 comparison ops, and/or/not, and literals, consumed by transition.ex for exclusive-gateway conditions. Its own moduledoc says 'A fuller expression surface, if a later stage needs one, EXTENDS this module rather than replacing it.' So S6 expr requirements must EXTEND expr.ex, never rewrite it. Genuinely missing and hard-rejected today via @unsupported_call_markers: arithmetic (+ - * / %), the `in` membership operator, ternary ?:, CEL macros (has/matches/all/exists/exists_one), type-conversion functions (int/uint/double/string/bool/bytes/duration/timestamp), collection functions (size/map/filter), list/map literals, list indexing, and any structured error surface (R-Co src/expr/error.zig) -- today every failure collapses to false via the catch-false rule, which REQ-050's EE-05 AC4 REQUIRES for gateway conditions, so a structured error surface must NOT break that gateway contract. src/expr/benchmark.zig deliberately gets no Elixir equivalent -- say so explicitly rather than silently dropping it. (2) OBSERVABILITY: lib/letflow/routers/metrics.ex and routers/audit.ex exist as ROUTE SHELLS from REQ-078 (done S4); metrics.ex's own moduledoc says 'S6 observability is the owning stage for Letflow's metrics subsystem ... it is a placeholder shape, not the design' and it deliberately diverges from R-Co on three axes (authenticated not anonymous, per-tenant not global, JSON not Prometheus text) -- an S6 metrics requirement must decide explicitly whether to keep or reverse each of those three divergences, not silently pick one. audit.ex is served from EventStore.read_global/1 and its moduledoc records that Letflow has NO audit_entries table (R-Co has one at src/obs/audit.zig:107), so resource_type is hardcoded 'instance' and before_state/after_state are ALWAYS null -- an S6 audit requirement closes exactly that gap. GET /instances/:id/timeline exists from REQ-080 (done S4). :AuditRead and :MetricsRead permissions already exist in lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex. lib/letflow/engine/lua_script_audit.ex + table lua_script_execution_audit exist (REQ-058/153/158) as a NARROW separate trail -- do not conflate it with the general audit log. There are ZERO :telemetry.execute call sites in the entire codebase and no telemetry_metrics/prometheus dep in mix.exs. OBS-05 (DLQ) is ALREADY OWNED by REQ-176/177/178 -- this batch must NOT redraft it. (3) REPOSITORY: three separate code sites already define the injectable seam a real service catalog must satisfy -- lib/letflow/definitions/service_scope_validator.ex:59-60 and :108 (REQ-031, takes an injected Lookup struct of function values, says a DB-backed ServiceCatalog 'belongs to stage S6'), lib/letflow/definitions/solution_pack.ex:35/:271/:512 (service_catalog_entries hard-fails with {:error, :unsupported_pack_section}), lib/letflow/engine/pin_resolver.ex:27 ('SCOPE GAP -- service_catalog (S6) and PLC-01 (unscoped) are not built'). SVC-04 service-catalog permissions already sit in the authz matrix (authorization.ex:190,383) with no backing subsystem. docs/migration/stage-4-api-surface.md:101 defers services.zig (417 lines) to S6. Canonicalisation exists only as promotion-plan canonicalisation in definitions/promotion_digest.ex (REQ-036) -- R-Co's general canonicaliser.zig is unported. process_module_catalog is entirely greenfield. A service-catalog requirement must state which of those three seams it satisfies and MUST make solution_pack.ex's hard-fail path reachable-or-explicitly-still-deferred rather than leaving it dangling. (4) SCHEDULER: essentially nothing exists -- :TIMER is in the graph node enum with one definition-time validator (definitions/graph.ex check_timer_duration/1, CHK-12) but transition.ex:283 sends :TIMER into the catch-all UNHANDLED dispatch branch, and engine/task_activation.ex:338-339 cancel_pending_timers/2 is an explicitly-named NO-OP STUB documented as the SCH-03 hook owned by S6 (called from engine.ex:1177). engine.ex:234-242 records the deferral. event_retention_policies table + EventStore.archive/1 exist (REQ-026) but are MANUALLY INVOKED ONLY -- no periodic runner. application.ex's supervision tree has NO periodic/cron process of any kind. (5) SECRETS: zero. No table, no crypto-at-rest, no redaction subsystem, no reference resolution. (6) ORDERING: zero from src/ordering/. Beware false positives: api/pagination.ex's 'cursor' is HTTP list pagination (REQ-067), and event_store/instance_sequence.ex + the global_seq column (REQ-023/025/026) are the event store's own sequencing, NOT R-Co's ordering subsystem.

TWO BLOCKERS NEED THEIR OWN DECISION/DESIGN REQUIREMENTS, drafted the way S5 handled its open questions (REQ-148/149/150 -- read those three entries in full first as the model for shape, depth and 'produce a DECIDED answer including a decided no' framing). (a) SCHEDULER FIRING ARCHITECTURE: no docs/migration/decisions/*.md record settles what fires a deferred timer (Oban vs a supervised per-timer process vs a polling GenServer); mix.exs has neither Oban nor Quantum. The first batch cited this as its reason for deferring scheduler. It is now MUCH more tractable than 'wide open', and the draft must say so: R-Co's SCH-02 (docs/requirements.yaml, RELEASED) specifies the mechanism concretely -- a background poller at a configurable interval (default 5s, env-var configurable), selecting status=PENDING AND fire_at <= NOW(), firing each due timer in a SINGLE transaction that marks it FIRED and appends the instance event, and in clustered deployments taking a PostgreSQL ADVISORY LOCK on the timer id before processing (skip if unavailable, released at commit). Edge cases are specified too (DB unavailable -> rollback, stays PENDING, retried next poll; a timer due between polls fires next poll, max latency = interval + jitter). SCH-06 adds jitter, SCH-05 requires overdue timers carry fired_late:true with scheduled-vs-actual timestamps and that NONE is skipped or double-fired. So the decision requirement's job is to choose Letflow's BEAM-idiomatic realisation of that specified behaviour (and whether to add an Oban dependency at all) with REVIEWER sign-off, NOT to reopen the polling-vs-push question R-Co already answered. Also read R-Co src/design/iss0618-scheduler-lock-and-error-signaling.md and scheduler-concurrency-epic3.md, which record real operational failures of R-Co's own implementation -- a port that repeats them is a bad port. (b) SECRETS BACKEND: docs/migration/stage-6-operational-cross-cutting.md's own Decisions section says 'Likely needs a decision file for src/secrets specifically (secret storage/retrieval backend choice) -- defer until this stage starts.' The stage is starting, so that file must now be written by its own requirement. R-Co's EXP-501 states the target shape: per-tenant secrets under ENVELOPE ENCRYPTION (data keys wrapped by a host KMS/env master key), resolved BY REFERENCE at execution, values never appearing in definitions/logs/traces, and the module owning webhook HMAC keys. Note the direct collision to flag: REQ-181/183 (already pending, this same stage) have webhook subscriptions storing a HASHED secret and doing HMAC signing with it -- a secrets subsystem that 'owns webhook HMAC keys' per EXP-501 must state explicitly how it relates to REQ-181's already-specified hashed-secret storage, either superseding it with a stated migration path or deliberately leaving it alone with a reason. Do not let two requirements in one stage silently specify two different homes for the same key material. Read R-Co src/design/exp-05-secrets-module.md, fix-iss0112-secret-ref.md, iss-0076-secrets-table-migration-fix.md, and iss0635-gh616-webhook-secret-ref-migration.md (that last one is literally R-Co migrating webhook secrets to secret references -- direct precedent).

Every new requirement carries the full existing schema -- id, title, owner, status: pending, stage: S6, description, >=2 (aim 4-8) concrete verifiable acceptance_criteria, depends_on -- matching the prose style, depth and R-Co-path-citation habit of the existing S5 and first-batch-S6 entries. Read several in full before writing. Do NOT add an impl_order field or a placeholder value: ORCH assigns it in Step 3 from register_task's real response. Per TASK_QUEUE.md, an invented impl_order doubles as a working /tasks/<id>/ URL addressing an unrelated real task -- this has already caused a wrong task to be closed once (ISS-0092/GH#314).

Size each requirement to ONE agent turn and chain with depends_on rather than writing oversized entries. Follow the CORE/ROUTE SPLIT precedent this very stage already established and that REQ-VALIDATOR enforced on the first batch: REQ-176 (schema+context, 'no route or controller file is added') then REQ-178 (route layer atop it); REQ-181 then REQ-182; REQ-183 then REQ-184. Any S6 subsystem here that needs both a core and an HTTP surface (service catalog / services.zig, metrics, audit, secrets management, scheduler admin) MUST be split the same way, with the core requirement's acceptance criteria including the 'no route or controller file is added or modified, confirmed by git diff --stat scoped to this requirement's commits' clause.
